## AGY-25  (AUDIT FIXES, **P0/P1**) — resolve 10 defects a Claude adversarial audit CONFIRMED in your WS-VECTOR code  **[DONE]**
**Who:** you (Python + bash + SQL). **When:** NEXT — these are real, verified bugs in code you shipped (each independently code-traced + verified). Claude already fixed 2 (redact.py unquoted-secret leak + mios_db_config.py port fail-open) — do NOT redo those. Fix these 10:
**HIGH:**
1. **`verbcatalog.py` ~148-215 — the `db_authoritative` sentinel is a NO-OP.** The T-126 "Database Overlay" block runs UNCONDITIONALLY (only try/except-guarded), so with the sentinel FALSE (default) + pgvector up, the DB silently overlays/deletes verbs (`cat.pop` on is_active=false, overwrites sig/desc/tier/permission/cmd/params) — the returned catalog is NOT byte-identical to TOML. **Fix:** gate the entire T-126 overlay behind `is_db_authoritative()` so sentinel-FALSE returns the pure TOML catalog; keep only the shadow-compare (read-only) running when false.
2. **`embed_backfill.py` ~209-248 + `toolsearch.py` ~206-231 — emb_version PING-PONG on `verb`.** Backfill stamps `emb_version='nomic-768-v1'`; toolsearch treats a verb vector valid only if `emb_version == <sha256 fp>` and re-stamps fp. The two writers perpetually invalidate each other -> every core/common verb re-embeds every 15-min timer run (never idempotent). **Fix:** unify to ONE scheme on `verb.emb_version` (make backfill compute+store the SAME fingerprint toolsearch uses, OR make toolsearch honor backfill's version) so a stamped vector satisfies both readers.
3. **`agent_call.py` ~93/436/543 — token guard permanently WEDGES a session.** `_SESSION_TOKENS[session_id]` is cumulative-only, never windowed/reset; once a session crosses `conversation_token_ceil` (2M) `used > conv_ceil` raises `ValueError` on EVERY later dispatch for the process lifetime -> the user can never get another answer until daemon restart. **Fix:** make it a rolling window + graceful summarize (mirror `chat.py`'s `_budget_admit`/`_BUDGET_LEDGER`), not a permanent hard-raise.
**MEDIUM:**
4. **`mios_db_config.py` ~13/197 — `DIVERGENCES` counts read-observations, never resets** -> the health `config_divergences` gauge climbs unbounded on any persistent mismatch read on hot paths. **Fix:** track a SET of distinct divergent `scope.key`s (or reset per rebuild) so the gauge = number of divergent settings.
5. **`verbcatalog.py` ~234 — shadow-compare feeds the ALREADY-DB-OVERLAID `cat`** into `_compare_catalogs`, masking real TOML-vs-DB drift on shared verbs AND firing a false divergence for every TOML-only verb during partial migration. **Fix:** snapshot a PRE-overlay pure-TOML copy and compare THAT vs `db_cat`.
**LOW:**
6. `verbcatalog.py` ~225 — redundant SECOND blocking `psycopg.connect(connect_timeout=2)` on the sentinel-FALSE path (~4s dead wait when DB down). Skip/cache when not db_authoritative.
7. `toolsearch.py` ~231 — stamps `emb_model='qwen2.5-coder:1.5b'` on nomic-produced verb vectors (false provenance, disagrees with backfill's `nomic-embed-text`). Stamp the actual embed model.
8. `embed_backfill.py` ~243-249 — `embedded_count += 1` runs even when the degrade-open `mios_pg.execute()` UPDATE returned None (silent DB failure over-reported as success). Check the return; count only real writes.
9. `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` check 32 (~2707-2770) — "lossless" round-trip only diffs pkgs + phase ordinal/deps/stage; add `enable`/`layer`/`base_image_ref`/`section` + `debloat_profile.description` + `preset.debloat_profile_name` to the diff.
10. `materialize-build-ctx.py` ~59 — same-ordinal `build_phase` tie-breaks by DB `id`, so an incremental re-seed sorts a new same-prefix script after older peers instead of lexically. **Fix:** `ORDER BY stage, ordinal NULLS LAST, script` (lexical), not `id`.
**Where/Done When:** fix each at the cited file:line; add/extend tests (`test_mios_db_config`/`test_mios_backfill`/`test_mios_verbcatalog`) to cover the fixed behavior; `just drift-gate` green; **stage only your files (never the Quadlets).**

**Who:** you (Python, agent-pipe). **When:** now or right after AGY-47 (server.py decomposition) — this adds two routes + a config writer. Claude is landing the CLIENT half in `usr/share/mios/configurator/mios.html` (inert/degrade-to-download until these routes exist), so ship these and the loop closes.
**What + How:** the Portal already embeds the configurator (`GET /portal/configurator` serves mios.html into the shell iframe), but mios.html can only save via browser download — there is NO server read/write of the SSOT. Add two routes:
- **`GET /portal/config`** → return the live LAYERED `mios.toml` (vendor<host<user) as `text/plain` TOML for the form to seed from. Reuse the existing read path (the `tomllib.load` the Portal already does for `[colors]`/`[ports]`, `mios_pipe/kernel/config.py`).
- **`POST /portal/config`** → body = raw TOML; validate it parses; PERSIST to the **user layer `~/.config/mios/mios.toml`** by default (host `/etc/mios/mios.toml` only when the session is a privileged/admin operator). Return a JSON status. **Persist-only — do NOT trigger `mios build`** (apply stays an explicit operator action).
- Add the **writer** to `mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` (currently read-only): write the correct layer file atomically (temp+rename), preserving SSOT cascade semantics.
- **Auth:** reuse the portal session (`_portal_authed`) + honor `[security].api_require_auth`; when unauthorized/disabled return 403/404 so the client gracefully falls back to browser-download (the client half is built to degrade).
- Wire the routes in `mios_pipe/routing/portal.py` + the thin `@app`/router entry in `server.py` (coordinate with your AGY-47 decomposition).
**Where:** `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` (writer), `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/routing/portal.py` (routes), `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/server.py` (wiring), a `test_mios_config_write.py`.
**Done When:** `GET /portal/config` returns the live TOML; `POST /portal/config` persists to `~/.config/mios/mios.toml` atomically, auth-gated, no build triggered; unauthorized → 403 so the client degrades to download; tests green; `just drift-gate` green. Stage only your files.
**OPEN (operator may adjust):** the write-layer default (per-user vs host), and whether a future 'Apply' action should trigger `mios build` (out of scope here — persist-only for now).

## AGY-57  (WS-DOTFILES / ADR-0010, **P2**) — the `kind` axis + `json-merge` mode (Windows Terminal / VS Code settings.json)  **[DONE]**
> **[DONE by Claude on main -- ea756065] kind axis + json-merge landed; verified check PASS 9, foreign-key-preserving, fail-loud exit 3.**
**Who:** you (Python). **When:** first of the two; parallel-safe (mios-theme-render is Claude-owned but idle).
**What + How:**
1. **kind axis:** add optional `kind` to `[dotfiles.registry.<surface>]` ∈ `template|json-merge|ini-merge|registry|skip` (absent ⇒ `template`). `_load_surfaces` (~L46) returns a namedtuple `_Surface(name,template,target,section,kind,fixture,policy)` (so `_entry`/template call sites are untouched); it VALIDATES: unknown kind ⇒ `exit 3` (same posture as the missing-template `exit 3` at L64-67); a merge kind MUST declare `fixture.base` + `fixture.expected` else `exit 3` (no ungated merge surface — preserves the no-vacuous-green stance).
2. **dispatch:** module-level `_KINDS = {kind: (derive_fn, live_apply_fn)}`. `cmd_render`/`cmd_check` select `derive_fn` by `surface.kind` and keep the uniform shape `derive(surface,merged)->committed_target_bytes` then write/byte-diff (check NEVER reads a live foreign file — offline PR gate). `cmd_apply` selects `live_apply_fn`. template kind = today's `_render_text` whole-file (cmd_apply L343-393 UNCHANGED).
3. **json-merge derive/apply:** `owned = _render_text(tmpl, _resolved_for(merged,section))` is a MiOS-owned JSON SUBTREE (only the keys MiOS projects — e.g. VS Code `workbench.colorCustomizations` or WT `profiles.defaults`/`schemes[]`). `derive = json_merge(owned, fixture.base)`; `apply = json_merge(owned, LIVE dest) -> write-back + backup`. `json_merge`: (a) `_jsonc_to_json(base)` — a STRING-AWARE comment/trailing-comma strip that never mangles `https://` or a `//` inside a string value; if base won't parse ⇒ `exit 2`, write NOTHING (never corrupt an unreadable file). (b) `json.loads` (insertion-ordered). (c) deep-merge: recurse dicts; a MiOS-owned leaf/array wins (arrays REPLACED wholesale at the owned pointer — index-merge is unsafe); any key MiOS does NOT emit is byte-preserved. (d) `json.dump` with base indent, `ensure_ascii=False`.
4. **drift-gating for merge surfaces:** the surface declares `fixture.base` (a checked-in canonical base) + `fixture.expected` (the expected merged output); `check` = `derive(owned, fixture.base)` byte-diff `fixture.expected`. Add a proof `json-merge` surface (e.g. `vscode-colors`: a small MiOS-owned colorCustomizations template + a `fixture.base` that already contains a FOREIGN key + the `fixture.expected` with that foreign key preserved).
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-theme-render` (`_load_surfaces`, `_KINDS`, `_jsonc_to_json`/`_json_deep_merge`, cmd_render/check/apply branch), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (the new surface + `kind`/`fixture`), a new `.tmpl`, a fixtures dir (e.g. `usr/share/mios/theme/fixtures/`).
**Done When:** the 8 existing surfaces render/check **byte-identical** (kind defaults template — prove with the render byte-diff); the `json-merge` proof surface merges owned keys into `fixture.base` PRESERVING the foreign key (test); `check` gates it via the fixture; `apply` into a live temp target preserves foreign + writes a backup; unknown-kind / missing-fixture ⇒ `exit 3`; unparseable base ⇒ `exit 2` no-write; `capture` still template-only; `just drift-gate` green. Stage only your files.

## AGY-58  (WS-DOTFILES / ADR-0010, **P2**) — `ini-merge` mode + a `gitconfig-live` surface (UNBLOCK gitconfig live-apply)  **[DONE]**
> **[DONE by Claude on main -- 8f52ccfb] ini-merge + gitconfig-live landed; check PASS 10, live-apply preserves credential/signing/remotes + seeds owned + backup. gitconfig live-apply UNBLOCKED.**
**Who:** you (Python). **When:** after AGY-57 (needs the `kind` dispatch + `_KINDS`).
**What + How:**
1. **ini-merge derive/apply:** `_parse_ini(text)` keeps an ORDERED line-model + a `{(section,subsection,key)->line_idx}` index (preserves `#`/`;` comments + `[section "subsection"]` quoting). `owned_kv = _parse_ini(_render_text(gitconfig.tmpl))` — so MiOS owns EXACTLY the keys the template emits (`user.name/email`, `core.editor`, `init.defaultBranch`, `pull.rebase`, `alias.{co,br,ci,st}`). `_ini_upsert` per owned key: ABSENT in base ⇒ seed (append the section block if the section is absent); PRESENT ⇒ replace value in place per policy. Everything NOT in `owned_kv` (`credential`, `user.signingkey`, `commit.gpgsign`, remotes) is byte-preserved. Subsectioned keys keyed on `(section,subsection)` so they never collide; leave foreign multivar keys untouched (owned set is single-valued).
2. **merge write policy** `seed-or-enforce` (default for gitconfig, safety-first): per owned key — ABSENT ⇒ write (seed); PRESENT + `operator_set(key)` ⇒ write (enforce the operator's explicit SSOT choice); PRESENT + NOT `operator_set` ⇒ SKIP (never stomp an existing foreign value with a vendor default). `operator_set = mios_toml.load_merged(sec,key) != mios_toml.load_vendor(sec,key)` AND non-empty.
3. **gitconfig-live surface (NEW, ADDITIVE):** `kind=ini-merge`, `policy=seed-or-enforce`, `template` REUSES `usr/share/mios/theme/templates/gitconfig.tmpl` VERBATIM (the rendered template's `[section] key=value` lines ARE the ownership manifest AND the values), `apply.target.linux="~/.gitconfig"`, `apply.target.windows="%USERPROFILE%/.gitconfig"`, `fixture.base`/`fixture.expected` = a small canonical gitconfig pair. The EXISTING `gitconfig` surface (etc/skel/.gitconfig, kind=template, NO apply.target) stays BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is the safe unblock of the live-apply Claude withheld (whole-file overwrite would clobber the user credential/signing/remotes; ini-merge sets only the ~9 owned keys).
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-theme-render` (`_parse_ini`/`_ini_upsert`/`_operator_set` + the ini-merge `_KINDS` entry), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (the `gitconfig-live` surface), a fixtures pair.
**Done When:** the existing `gitconfig` (template) surface is byte-identical; `apply gitconfig-live` into a live `~/.gitconfig` seeded with a FOREIGN `[credential]`/`user.signingkey`/remote PRESERVES them (assert) while setting the owned keys; `seed-or-enforce` SKIPS an existing foreign `user.email` unless operator_set; `check` gates via the fixture; a backup is written on change; unknown/missing-fixture ⇒ `exit 3`; `just drift-gate` green. Stage only your files.

### AGY-84 REFINEMENT (Claude, VERIFIED against HEAD 3551d6d5) -- do NOT naive-emit ~500 vars
The drift-check "referenced but NOT emitted (a consumer would lose its var)" is OVER-BROAD. I read two representatives and confirmed the premise is false for the bulk:
- `server.py:804` `MIOS_ACI_HEAD_FRAC` = `_cfg_num(_ACI_TOML,"MIOS_ACI_HEAD_FRAC","head_frac",0.6,float)` -> reads `[aci].head_frac` from mios.toml SSOT with default; env is an OPTIONAL override. Consumer canNOT lose its var.
- `test_mios_template.py:48` `MIOS_NONEXISTENT_ENV` = deliberate test sentinel ("default absent -> fallback"). Must NEVER be emitted.
**Fix the CHECK to its true intent (flag only a var a consumer would GENUINELY lose), by category:**
- **A. SSOT-section reads (bulk):** `_cfg_num`/`_cfg_bool`/`_cfg_str`/`_toml_section(...)` with an env-name arg AND a default -> COMPLIANT (var IS SSOT-sourced). Recognize these; do not flag. This is most of server.py / mios_pipe/**/config.py / kernel.
- **B. test/negative sentinels:** anything referenced ONLY under `test_*.py`, `tests/`, `*-negatives.sh`, or the `38-ssot-lint.sh` fixtures (MIOS_NONEXISTENT_ENV, MIOS_NO_SUCH_VAR_XYZ, MIOS_FOO, MIOS_FIXTURE_*, MIOS_AI_TEST_TEMP, MIOS_BENCH, MIOS_EGRESS_TOOL, MIOS_MTLS_TOOL, MIOS_AUTONOMOUS_PRIORITY, MIOS_ANSWER_CHUNK_CHARS...) -> EXCLUDE from the scan.
- **C. regex prefix fragments:** trailing `_` or `__` captures (MIOS_A2O_, MIOS_AGENT_, MIOS_PORT_, MIOS_NATIVE_LOOP_, MIOS_DRIVE__, MIOS_COLS__, MIOS_CELL_H__ ...) -> tighten the extraction regex so it does NOT capture partial identifiers / `${MIOS_x_}${suffix}` interpolation stems.
- **D. Windows PowerShell vars:** any hit in `*.ps1` (Get-MiOS.ps1, build-mios.ps1, mios-pipeline.ps1) is a WinPS var -> NOT a Linux env key; userenv.sh (bash) neither can nor should emit it. Route to the PS globals.ps1 SSOT lane; EXCLUDE `.ps1` from the "must be emitted by userenv.sh" scan.
- **E. genuine residue:** after A-D, the SMALL set of real bash/systemd consumers that read `${MIOS_X}` with NO default and NO SSOT-section read -> THESE emit from the auto-derived key library (WS-NAME), sourced from mios.toml, reconciling MIOS_AI_VLLM_* <-> short MIOS_VLLM_*.
**Done (unchanged):** 0 GENUINE referenced-but-not-emitted; A-D no longer flagged; twins identical (drift-27); add a negative test PER category (a Cat-A `_cfg_num` var, a Cat-B sentinel, a Cat-D `.ps1` var) proving they're correctly NOT flagged, and one Cat-E var proving a real orphan IS flagged until emitted.

## AGY-89  (WS-RELTOP hardening, **P1**) -- globals.sh clobbers the SSOT image name (audit-confirmed)  **[DONE]**
**Who:** you (your WS-RELTOP/T-252 code). An independent audit found your credential-driven selection has a real latent bug + a misleading framing:
- **Bug (E1):** `automation/lib/globals.sh:109-113` -- the no-creds branch does `export MIOS_IMAGE_NAME="localhost/mios"` UNCONDITIONALLY. `common.sh` sources `userenv.sh` FIRST (ghcr from SSOT) then `globals.sh`, so on a no-creds host this OVERWRITES userenv's ghcr with localhost -- contradicting your own `common.sh:48-52` comment ("globals fills gaps") and the "userenv stays faithful to SSOT" claim. It also leaves `MIOS_IMAGE_NAME=localhost/mios` while `MIOS_IMAGE_REF` stays ghcr (`:=` at :116) -> an inconsistent name/ref pair. Harmless TODAY only because no reachable consumer pulls via `$MIOS_IMAGE_NAME` (consumers are display/legacy/CI-sources-userenv-directly) -- but a landmine: any future `bootc switch`/`podman pull "$MIOS_IMAGE_NAME"` after `common.sh` on a no-cred host -> `localhost/mios` -> crash.
- **Framing:** the real build path (`usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-driver:766`) HARDCODES `localhost/mios:latest` and never sources globals; the fresh Windows/Linux entry points never source globals either -> the credential-selection block is effectively dead on all fresh paths.
**Fix:** replace the whole `_has_registry_creds` if/else (`globals.sh:~101-113`) with a non-clobbering default: `: "${MIOS_IMAGE_NAME:=ghcr.io/mios-dev/mios}"` (MIOS_LOCAL_IMAGE already carries the localhost tag; keep credential gating only on a build-vs-publish DECISION, never on the image NAME).
- **E4 (twin parity):** `automation/lib/globals.ps1:62-92` respects `$env:MIOS_IMAGE_NAME` in BOTH branches while `globals.sh` forces localhost in the no-creds branch -> the two "SSOT" twins disagree on override semantics. Align them (both = non-clobbering `:=` default to ghcr, local tag via MIOS_LOCAL_IMAGE).
**Done:** no-creds host keeps `MIOS_IMAGE_NAME=ghcr.io/mios-dev/mios` (name/ref consistent); sh+ps1 twins equivalent; drift-gate (41/45 resolver-twin) stays green; add a negative test asserting a no-creds `common.sh` load does NOT downgrade MIOS_IMAGE_NAME to localhost.

## AGY-97  (WS-HARDEN / scurl correctness, **P1**) — fix the scurl binary-stream corruption + harden its arg-parser  **[DONE]**
**Who:** you (bash). **When:** next — this is a real DATA-CORRUPTION bug, not just hygiene.
**What + How:** `automation/lib/masking.sh` `scurl()` sets `is_binary` ONLY when it sees `-o/-O/--output`. But the build's dominant pattern is `curl … | tar` (stream to stdout, NO `-o`) — scurl classifies that as **text** and pipes the tarball through `mask_filter` (`sed -u`), **corrupting the binary stream**. (1) Fix classification: NEVER run `mask_filter` on a body destined for a pipe/download — only mask human-facing text (e.g. gate masking on stdout being a TTY, or drop mask_filter for any non-`-o` streamed body). (2) Harden the naive parser: it takes the FIRST `https?://` arg as the URL and misses `--output=FILE`, `--url X`, and mis-detects a `-H` header value that looks like a URL. (3) Add `automation/lib/test_masking.sh`: asserts a piped binary body is byte-identical (no sed mangling), a github URL gets the auth header AND the token is masked in TEXT output, and `--output=` is detected.
**Where:** `automation/lib/masking.sh`, new `automation/lib/test_masking.sh`, wire into the shell-test/lint gate.
**Done When:** `curl … | tar` through scurl is byte-identical to raw curl; parser handles the 3 edge cases; test green; `just drift-gate` green.

Add the explicit `WITH (m=16, ef_construction=64)` to every param-less HNSW index (idempotent — CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS already guards, so it is a no-op on existing DBs but pins intent), and unify the outlier emb_version width. Add a new `check_vector_schema_hygiene` to automation/38-drift-checks.sh (next free number, 63+) that greps every `USING hnsw` line and fails if any lacks the canonical params, and asserts every `emb vector(768)` column has sibling `emb_model`+`emb_version`.
**Where:** usr/share/mios/postgres/schema-init.sql, automation/38-drift-checks.sh. **Done When:** `psql -f schema-init.sql` re-applies idempotently (no-op on an existing DB); the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED on a fixture where an HNSW index is stripped of its params or an emb column loses provenance; `just drift-gate` passes.

## AGY-282  (WS-BAKE, **P1**) — Nested-build mount + scratch cleanup trap (mount-leak hardening)  **[DONE]**

On a failure mid-build (both are `set -euo pipefail`) they exit WITHOUT tearing down the inner store's overlay mounts or purging `$SCRATCH` — on a retried CI runner this leaks overlay/loopback mounts and fills the runner disk (a documented WS-BAKE failure mode). In `mios-bake-group` respect the existing `MIOS_BAKE_BOUND_IMAGES=0` early-exit (L47-50) so the trap is a no-op there. Reference the existing partial cleanup at `mios-bake-group` L58/L140.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh`, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-group`.
**Done When:** `bash -n` clean on both; the trap fires on both success and forced-failure paths (test with an injected `false`) and never alters the propagated exit code; `${SCRATCH:?}` guard present so an unset var can't `rm -rf /`; `just drift-gate` green; stage only the two scripts.

It SELECTs enabled Linux-scoped rows from `account` (`WHERE enabled AND os_targets IN ('both','linux')`, same predicate as `mios-account-sync`'s `query_db_accounts`) and writes one JSON User Record per user to `/run/userdb/<name>.user` (runtime tmpfs, since the DB is the runtime SSOT and `/usr` is immutable) following systemd.io/USER_RECORD (`userName`, `uid`, `gid`, `realName`←display, `homeDirectory`←home_dir, `shell`, `disposition:"regular"`; hashed secret in a `.user-privileged` companion, mode 0600, NEVER plaintext). Idempotent: only rewrite when content changed (mirror materialize-user-config's compare-before-write at `:160-176`). Gate the whole run on `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED` like `automation/17-accounts-db.sh`; fail-open (log + exit 0) when psycopg/DB is absent so offline boot is unaffected. This is a PROJECTION (bake/sync), keeping Postgres out of the login critical path per the doc's libnss-pgsql caution.
**Where:** usr/libexec/mios/mios-userdb-render. **Done When:** `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-userdb-render` passes; a dry-run with a mocked cursor (fixture rows) emits a valid User Record JSON that `python -c "import json;json.load(...)"` accepts and whose `userName`/`uid`/`homeDirectory` match the fixture; running twice on unchanged input writes nothing the second pass.

## AGY-340 [DONE] (WS-DB, **P3**) — Use the DB-owned uid_alloc sequence instead of the hardcoded 1000 gid fallback in account sync  **[DONE]**
**Who:** you (Python + SQL). **What+How:** `schema-init.sql:795-807` defines `SEQUENCE uid_alloc` + `allocate_uid()`/`allocate_gid()` precisely so ids are DB-owned, but `mios-account-sync:180` still falls back to a hardcoded `gid = db_user["gid"] or 1000` (and `useradd` at `:214-228` inherits it), which silently collides with the allocator and violates the everything-db-driven V4 intent. When a row has NULL uid/gid, allocate via the DB (`SELECT allocate_gid()` / `allocate_uid()` through `mios-pg-query`) and persist it back onto the `account` row (UPDATE), so ids are assigned ONCE in the DB and every projection (Linux useradd, AGY-334 userdb, AGY-339 Windows manifest) reads the same value. Keep the change additive and idempotent (only allocate when the column is NULL). Also drop the literal `1000` fallback from `query_db_accounts`'s default (`:180`) — an unresolved id is an error to log, not a magic default (NO-HARDCODE spirit).
**Where:** usr/libexec/mios/mios-account-sync. **Done When:** `python -m py_compile` passes; a stubbed-`mios-pg-query` unit test shows a NULL-gid row triggers exactly one `allocate_gid()` + one write-back UPDATE and reuses the stored id on the next pass; no `1000` literal remains in the id path; `just drift-gate` green.

The crate is the strangler facade: `miosd build` first shells out to the unchanged automation/build.sh loop, but reads the phase list, exit-code policy and per-step timing through a typed `Phase` model so individual phases can be rerouted to native code later without changing the outer call. ### AGY-1011 -- Statically link miosd (musl) so one binary runs identically at build, in-image, and in the firstboot-tier  (WS-LANG-AUTO | P3 | S)
**What+How:** The Containerfile builds miosd with FROM docker.io/library/rust:slim (glibc) and copies /miosd into /usr/libexec/mios/miosd. A glibc-dynamic binary risks libc drift between the builder and the (potentially distroless/firstboot-tier) runtime and cannot be reused as a host build tool on other bases. Switch the rust-builder to a static target (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) with a pinned rustls/no-openssl feature set, so the same artifact runs at build time, inside the image, and in the shrunk firstboot-tier without a libc dependency.
**Where:** `Containerfile, src/mios-rs/Cargo.toml, src/mios-rs/miosd/, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml`
**Done When:** miosd is a static musl binary (ldd reports 'not a dynamic executable'), runs on the base image and in a distroless/firstboot context, image size does not regress, and cargo test + drift-gate green.  **Why:** As miosd becomes the executor for postcheck/renderers and the firstboot-tier deliberately strips whales, a glibc-dynamic build is a portability and reproducibility hazard; a static musl binary is the correct target for a cross-context build tool.  **Dep:** Unify the two Rust workspaces and make the Containerfile build+ship every native crate

### AGY-1054 -- Migrate the 70 systemd unit ExecStart references onto ported binaries preserving degrade-open prefixes, gated by an ExecStart-resolves drift-check  (WS-LANGX | P2 | M)

Add a drift-check that every `ExecStart*=/usr/libexec/mios/...` token resolves to an existing+executable path in the built tree, and audit each ported unit keeps its `-`/`+` semantics.

**Done When:** drift-check flags any dangling or non-executable ExecStart libexec path; all 70 units resolve post-port; ported units retain identical paths and degrade-open prefixes; gate green.  **Why:** A path rename or a dropped `-` prefix during a port silently converts a soft-fail provisioner into a boot-blocking one; the tree has no gate today asserting ExecStart targets even exist.  **Dep:** Extend the Containerfile rust-builder to compile the tools/native workspace and COPY every release binary into /usr/libexec/mios

### AGY-1057 -- Port the atomic bootc/OCI-delta swap family (bootc-switch-from-build.sh, mios-oci-delta-service.sh, mios-stage-oci-archive) to a transactional miosd bootc-apply subcommand  (WS-LANGX | P1 | L)

**Done When:** characterization tests cover sentinel present/absent/corrupt and interrupted-swap; idempotent with rollback on failure; units call miosd; gate green.  **Why:** Atomicity here is the difference between a self-updating host and an unbootable one -- exactly the class that deserves a compiled, tested implementation over string-parsing shell.  **Dep:** Stand up the golden-master parity harness (trycmd + insta) for libexec verb ports

### AGY-1058 -- Port the security-enrollment tools (mios-enroll-secure-boot, mios-clevis-luks-gen, mios-keyring-autounlock, selinux-init) to fail-closed Rust binaries  (WS-LANGX | P2 | L)
**What+How:** These un-targeted bash tools sit on the security path: mios-enroll-secure-boot enrolls the akmods MOK via mokutil so signed NVIDIA/ZFS kmods load under Secure Boot; mios-clevis-luks-gen binds LUKS via clevis; mios-keyring-autounlock handles keyring autounlock; selinux-init initializes SELinux. Unlike the degrade-open provisioners, silent failure here weakens Secure Boot / disk encryption. Port to small static Rust units that FAIL-CLOSED on the security assertion (non-zero, audit-logged) rather than degrade-open, with characterization tests over mokutil/clevis fixtures.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/{mios-enroll-secure-boot,mios-clevis-luks-gen,mios-keyring-autounlock,selinux-init}, src/mios-rs/miosd`
**Done When:** each replacement matches bash on golden fixtures, provably fails closed on the security assertion, and emits an audit trail; gate green.  **Why:** Degrade-open is correct for AI provisioners but wrong for MOK/LUKS/SELinux; compiling these lets us make the fail-closed contract explicit and testable instead of implicit in shell exit codes.  **Dep:** Stand up the golden-master parity harness (trycmd + insta) for libexec verb ports

**What+How:** The covered title only ports flatpaks-manage.sh + flatpak-launch. ### AGY-1060 -- Port the root-as-git-tree machinery (git-root-init.sh, mios-sync-to-root, verify-root.sh) to a miosd root subcommand  (WS-LANGX | P2 | M)
**What+How:** Per the '/ IS $ROOT' design: verify-root.sh is an early-boot composefs/ostree integrity check (mios-verify-root.service, basic.target); git-root-init.sh initializes the deployed / as a git working tree of the local repo; mios-sync-to-root applies the war-room ext4 replica LIVE onto the system root, GATED to mutable MiOS-DEV roots only (never an immutable bootc/ostree root). **Done When:** mutable-vs-immutable gating is preserved and tested; verify-root fails closed on integrity mismatch; units call miosd; characterization tests pass; gate green.  **Why:** These underpin the self-updating-tree architecture and mutate the live root; a gating regression in mios-sync-to-root could write onto an immutable root, so it warrants compiled guarantees.  **Dep:** Stand up the golden-master parity harness (trycmd + insta) for libexec verb ports

### AGY-1061 -- Fold the container build-if-missing firstboot bootstraps (mios-agents-firstboot.sh, mios-forgejo-runner-firstboot.sh, mios-webtools-firstboot.sh) into one shared idempotent Rust provisioner  (WS-LANGX | P3 | M)
**What+How:** Three uncovered bash firstboots share one pattern -- check if a podman image exists, `podman build` it if missing, degrade-open: mios-agents-firstboot.sh (A2O super-container, ExecStartPre), mios-forgejo-runner-firstboot.sh (register-once runner token), mios-webtools-firstboot.sh (crawl4ai + firecrawl stack). ### AGY-1062 -- Add a hermetic fake-root / recorded-invocation characterization harness for side-effectful firstboot and provisioner ports  (WS-LANGX | P2 | L)

## WS-DEBT-PY -- Harden the 122 usr/libexec python tools + tools/*.py (typed, packaged, tested)  (AGY-1066..AGY-1105, 40 tasks)

### AGY-1066 -- Package the 122 libexec Python tools as an installable `mios_tools` module with pyproject + entry-points, killing the 52 sys.path hacks  (WS-DEBT | P1 | L)
**What+How:** There is NO pyproject.toml/setup.py anywhere in the tree (verified) and 52 files under usr/libexec/mios do `sys.path.insert(0, '.../usr/lib/mios')` to reach the shared resolver. Create usr/lib/mios/pyproject.toml declaring a `mios_tools` package (PEP 621, hatchling/setuptools backend) that owns mios_toml.py, mios_env.py, mios_db_config.py as importable submodules, and register the extensionless hyphenated tools (mios-a2a-discover, mios-ai-tag, mios-hardcode-lint, ...) as `[project.scripts]` console entry-points mapping `mios-a2a-discover` -> `mios_tools.a2a_discover:main`. Strangler-fig: land the package + entry-points FIRST while the tools still live at their current paths (build installs the package into the image site-packages), then in follow-ups flip each tool's body to `from mios_tools import config`. Keep the current path shim as a thin `import runpy; runpy.run_module('mios_tools.<x>')` launcher until parity is proven, then delete the loose script.
**Where:** `usr/lib/mios/pyproject.toml (new), usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_env.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_db_config.py, usr/libexec/mios/* (122 python tools), automation/*.sh (install phase)`
**Done When:** pyproject.toml builds a wheel; `python -m build` + `pip install` exposes `import mios_tools.config` with NO sys.path.insert; at least the 3 shared modules import cleanly as `mios_tools.*`; `just drift-gate` green; explicit-path staged (no git add -A).  **Why:** The package boundary is the strangler-fig façade for the whole WS-DEBT campaign: every later port (typed models, mypy, Rust ports) needs importable modules. Removes the 52 fragile sys.path hacks and the SourceFileLoader workarounds they force.

### AGY-1067 -- Build a trycmd golden-master characterization harness capturing every SSOT `--check` projector's stdout/stderr/exit-code before any Rust port  (WS-DEBT | P1 | M)
**What+How:** The projectors (generate-cosign-policy.py, generate-uki-cmdline.py, generate-egress-firewall.py, generate-pod-quadlets.py, generate-names-registry.py, compile-templates.py) all expose a deterministic `--check` drift mode (verified: they diff a generated artifact vs the tracked file and exit 1 on drift). Before porting ANY of them, add a Rust `trycmd` harness under tools/native/mios-projector-golden/ that runs each current .py projector against a frozen fixture mios.toml and records stdout+stderr+exit into .trycmd/.md snapshot files. This is the parity oracle: a ported Rust binary must reproduce these byte-for-byte. Capture BOTH the generate mode (the emitted file bytes) and the --check mode (the diff/OK message). Add a `cargo test -p mios-projector-golden` step to the Justfile drift-gate.
**Where:** `tools/native/mios-projector-golden/ (new crate), tools/generate-cosign-policy.py, tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py, tools/generate-egress-firewall.py, tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py, tools/generate-names-registry.py, tools/compile-templates.py, Justfile (drift-gate recipe ~line 81)`
**Done When:** `cargo test -p mios-projector-golden` passes with committed .trycmd fixtures for >=6 projectors; the snapshots capture exit code + full stdout/stderr; harness runs in `just drift-gate`; fixtures are byte-frozen (insta/trycmd accept workflow documented in the crate README).  **Why:** Golden-master/characterization testing is the non-negotiable prerequisite for safe strangler-fig ports: without a recorded oracle, a Rust rewrite of a security projector (policy.json, kernel cmdline) could silently diverge. Turns the recurring quadlet-digest/SSOT-projection drift into accept/review snapshots.

### AGY-1068 -- Consolidate the fragmented tools/native crates into ONE cargo workspace with a committed Cargo.lock SSOT and cargo-deny/cargo-audit gates  (WS-DEBT | P1 | M)
**What+How:** tools/native/Cargo.toml declares a workspace with ONLY 3 members (mios-drift-runner, mios-version-check, mios-wallpaperd), yet 5 more crate dirs exist and build out-of-tree: generate-names-registry, mios-aiplane-lint, mios-bake-plan, mios-ssot-lint, mios-ssot-walk (verified by ls). Add all 8 as workspace members so they share one Cargo.lock and target dir. Add a deny.toml (advisories DB, license allow-list matching the FOSS posture, banned/duplicate-crate rules) and wire `cargo deny check` + `cargo audit` as new drift-gate steps. Commit Cargo.lock as a reproducibility SSOT (SBOM-not-hardcode: dependency digests recorded at build, not hand-pinned). Add `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` alongside.
**Where:** `tools/native/Cargo.toml, tools/native/Cargo.lock, tools/native/deny.toml (new), tools/native/{generate-names-registry,mios-aiplane-lint,mios-bake-plan,mios-ssot-lint,mios-ssot-walk}/Cargo.toml, Justfile, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml`

A single workspace + deny/audit is the security foundation every subsequent Rust port lands into, and gives bash-replacements the vetting bash never had.

### AGY-1069 -- Eliminate os.system() command-injection sites in mios-models and mios-v2v-import  (WS-DEBT | P1 | S)
**What+How:** Two shell-injection surfaces confirmed: usr/libexec/mios/mios-models:46 `os.system(f"python3 {fb}")` interpolates a path into a shell string, and usr/libexec/mios/mios-v2v-import:88 `os.system(cmd_str)` runs a fully string-built virt-v2v command. Replace both with `subprocess.run([...], check=...)` passing an argv LIST (no shell), so no value is ever re-parsed by /bin/sh. For mios-models use `subprocess.run([sys.executable, fb], ...)`. For mios-v2v-import, build the command as a list from the start rather than a joined string. Preserve degrade-open behavior (mios-v2v-import already `shutil.which('virt-v2v')` guards). Add a ruff/grep drift-check banning `os.system(` in usr/libexec/mios.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-models (line ~46), usr/libexec/mios/mios-v2v-import (line ~88)`
**Done When:** No `os.system(` remains under usr/libexec/mios (grep clean); both tools invoke subprocess with an argv list; behavior unchanged for present/absent binary; a drift-gate fails on any reintroduced os.system; `just drift-gate` green.  **Why:** os.system with an f-string/joined string is textbook shell injection on an OS-plane tool — the exact bug-class the hardening campaign exists to eliminate, and cheap to fix.

### AGY-1070 -- Harden SQL identifier interpolation in the sqlite CLIs with a validated table allowlist  (WS-DEBT | P1 | M)
**What+How:** f-string interpolation of table names into SQL confirmed at usr/libexec/mios/mios-cache-clear:176 (`DELETE FROM {t}`), mios-owui-apply-knowledge:143 (`PRAGMA table_info({table})`) and :214 (`SELECT 1 FROM {tbl}`), and mios-owui-bootstrap-admin:313 (dynamic column list into INSERT). These are structural identifiers (params can't bind identifiers in sqlite), so wrap each in a strict validator: assert the identifier matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` AND is a member of an explicit allowlist set derived from the known schema, raising a typed error otherwise before it reaches execute(). Add a shared `mios_tools.sql.safe_ident()` helper (after packaging) so every call site uses one validated path. Extend the existing check_cli_sql_safety gate (referenced in automation/98-drift-checks.sh ~line 685; test_mios_cli_sqlsafety.py present) to fail on any new unvalidated f-string identifier into execute().
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-cache-clear (line ~176), usr/libexec/mios/mios-owui-apply-knowledge (lines ~143,214), usr/libexec/mios/mios-owui-bootstrap-admin (line ~313), usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_cli_sqlsafety.py, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** Every identifier splice passes through safe_ident() with regex+allowlist validation; a malformed table name raises before execute(); test_mios_cli_sqlsafety.py extended with a rejection case; the drift-gate fails on a new raw f-string identifier; `just drift-gate` green.  **Why:** sqlite identifier interpolation is the residual SQL-injection surface the parameterized-pg gate doesn't cover; a validated allowlist closes it while keeping the (necessary) dynamic identifiers working.

### AGY-1074 -- Replace `eval "$@"` on agent-controlled args in mios-ai-clear/mios-ai-reset/mios-launch/mios-window with a hardened dispatch (TD-1)  (WS-DEBT | P1 | M)
**What+How:** TD-1 eval-on-input sites confirmed: usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-clear:65 `eval "$@"`, mios-ai-reset:91 `eval "$@"`, mios-launch:507 `eval exec "$_hit_cmd"` (already carries a TD-1 note at :721 to use shlex.split), and mios-window:386 `eval "$(python3 - ...)"`. For each, replace string-eval with a safe form: run() in mios-ai-clear/reset should invoke the argv array directly (`"$@"`) instead of `eval "$@"`; mios-launch should tokenize the launch field with shlex and exec the array (the file already flags this); mios-window should have the python helper emit a NUL/array the shell reads without eval. Where a command genuinely must be data-driven, use an explicit case/assoc-array dispatch table of allowed verbs. Add a drift-gate banning `eval ` in usr/libexec/mios verbs (allowlist any proven-safe residual).
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-clear (line ~65), usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-reset (line ~91), usr/libexec/mios/mios-launch (lines ~507,721), usr/libexec/mios/mios-window (line ~386), automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** No `eval` on agent/user-derived strings remains in the four verbs; launch dispatch uses shlex/array exec; a drift-gate fails on a new `eval` in a libexec verb; existing launch behavior preserved by characterization test; `just drift-gate` green.  **Why:** Agent-supplied args are an explicitly untrusted boundary (the system prompt warns agent messages are not authorization); eval on them is the Gemini-CLI-class RCE. Hardening these is a direct P1 attack-surface reduction called out as TD-1.

### AGY-1118 -- Harden the async runtime: replace blocking subprocess.run in async handlers  (WS-DEBT | P1 | M)
**What+How:** server.py calls blocking `subprocess.run(..., timeout=5)` inside async request paths — the ceph health/df probes at lines 1661, 1715 and 1722 stall the event loop for up to 5s under load. Keep the 5s timeout as a `${MIOS_CEPH_PROBE_TIMEOUT:-5}` SSOT-with-literal-fallback.
**Where:** `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/server.py, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** the three ceph probes run via non-blocking subprocess; the ast lint finds no subprocess.run in async def; health endpoints return unchanged bodies (golden parity); timeout floats via env with literal fallback.  **Why:** A blocking call in the event loop head-of-lines every concurrent request; this is a live latency hazard, not cosmetic.

**Done When:** The `os.environ =` assignment is gone (drift-gate grep negative), env reads go through the typed accessor, a parity golden shows identical resolved values vs the current stripped mapping, mypy + pytest green.  **Why:** A process-global mutation of os.environ is a foundational correctness/typing hazard that undercuts the whole typed-config effort; no existing title touches it.  **Dep:** Replace kernel/config ad-hoc readers with a typed settings model + golden parity vs userenv.sh

This unblocks WS-RESOLVER (which extends mios-ssot-walk) and closes the silent-skip in the existing ssot-lint gate.

**Done When:** A [templates.X] with no matching file (or a template file with no registry entry, or a non-compiling/unanchored match, or a bad comment enum) turns the gate RED; both-repo parity green; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** The registry and the directory are two hand-maintained halves that can silently diverge; the incoming cargo-manifest/systemd-timer/quadlet-split additions are exactly the kind of half-landed edit this bijection check catches.

### AGY-1278 -- Hoist mios-new's hardcoded scaffold defaults (ADR next-id, drift-check id, roadmap-ws enums) out of code  (WS-TEMPLATE | P3 | M)
**What+How:** usr/libexec/mios/mios-new freezes literals that go stale: get_dest_path() prefixes new ADRs with `0012-` (line 64) though ADRs already run past 0011, render_template() hardcodes drift-check `{{id}}=99`, adr `{{status}}=accepted`, and roadmap-ws `{{theme}}='OS-Image & Build'`/`{{priority}}=P2`/`{{status}}=proposed`/`{{task_id}}=999`. Compute the ADR next-id by scanning usr/share/doc/mios/adr/ for max(NNNN)+1, and move the enum defaults into [templates.<type>].defaults in mios.toml so they are SSOT-defined, keeping the literal as a `${...:-LIT}`-style fallback. This is distinct from the dest-path routing table move (paths) -- it targets the interpolated default VALUES.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-new (render_template, get_dest_path), usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([templates.*])`
**Done When:** `mios new adr foo` assigns the true next sequential id; enum defaults resolve from [templates.*] with literal fallback; a golden fixture pins the computed output; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** Frozen `0012-` and `id=99` defaults are already stale and produce wrong scaffolds; defaults belong in SSOT per the operator-defined north star, not baked into the generator.  **Dep:** Move the hardcoded dest-path routing table into the [templates.*] SSOT

### AGY-1279 -- Add shebang, LF-only, and exec-bit conformance for script templates and fix templates' self-referential AI-related  (WS-TEMPLATE | P2 | M)
**What+How:** check-template-conformance only checks for an AI-hint header and substring markers; it never verifies a script's shebang, line endings, or exec bit, even though mios-new writes newline='\n' + chmod 0o755 (mios-new:186-193) and mios-template-engine only prepends a shebang when 'AI-hint:' is absent (mios-template-engine:37-43) -- inconsistent. The shipped templates also set AI-related to the TEMPLATE's own path (e.g. usr/share/mios/templates/python-tool line 3 points at /usr/share/mios/templates/python-tool), so every scaffold inherits a wrong AI-related. Extend conformance for bash/python/powershell types to require a first-line shebang + LF-only endings + (bootc) the exec bit, and rewrite the templates so the scaffolder emits an AI-related pointing at the produced file, not the template.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/check-template-conformance, usr/share/mios/templates/(python-tool,python-module,python-test,bash,bash-verb,bash-tool,drift-check,automation-step,powershell), usr/libexec/mios/mios-new`
**Done When:** A CRLF or shebang-less or non-executable script of a registered type turns the gate RED; scaffolded files carry an AI-related pointing at themselves; golden fixtures updated; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** Physical file properties (LF/shebang/exec-bit) are load-bearing for MiOS scripts on bootc yet completely unenforced, and the self-referential AI-related bug means every scaffold ships a wrong header the AI-tagger later trusts.

### AGY-1280 -- Reconcile Law-16 enforced_by to name both template gates and supply the missing compile-gate negative test  (WS-TEMPLATE | P2 | S)
**What+How:** mios.toml Law 16 (line 723) declares enforced_by="98-drift-checks.sh:check_template_conformance", omitting check_templates_compilation (Check 59), which is wired into the run at 98-drift-checks.sh:6336 and also enforces the one-template rule. Separately, check_template_conformance is listed in [testing.negative_coverage_exempt] (mios.toml:11513) but check_templates_compilation is NOT, so the negative-coverage gate expects a negative test for it that does not exist. Add check_templates_compilation to Law 16's enforced_by string and author the negatives entry (a deliberately invalid template must turn Check 59 RED). Mirror the mios.toml edits per Law 15 in mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git.
**Where:** `usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([laws] id=16 enforced_by, [testing.negative_coverage_exempt]), automation/97/98 negatives harness`
**Done When:** Law 16 enforced_by names both checks; a broken-template negative test drives Check 59 RED and is registered so check_negative_test_coverage is satisfied; both-repo parity green; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** The compile validator is a real Law 16 enforcer that is currently invisible to the law's own enforced_by metadata and to the negative-coverage accounting -- an integrity gap in the law-to-check registry.

### AGY-1281 -- Gate that generated=true templates are byte-reproducible from their generator  (WS-TEMPLATE | P3 | M)
**What+How:** [templates.quadlet] is generated=true (mios.toml:11441) -- meant to be produced by a generator, not hand-edited -- yet nothing verifies the shipped usr/share/mios/templates/quadlet matches what its generator would emit; this is the same drift class as the recurring 'broad git add strips @sha256 from generated Quadlets' hazard. Add a check (extend compile-templates or a dedicated gate) that, for every [templates.X] with generated=true, re-running its generator yields byte-identical output and RED on divergence. This also gives the coming .container/.pod/.network/.volume quadlet split a home as verified generated artifacts rather than hand-maintained files.
**Where:** `usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([templates.*] generated flag), usr/share/mios/templates/quadlet, tools/compile-templates.py, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** Editing a generated=true template so it diverges from generator output turns the gate RED; regenerating restores green; the quadlet-split scaffolds are covered; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** generated=true is asserted but never verified, so a hand-edit or a broad git add can silently desync a generated template from its source-of-truth generator.  **Dep:** Split the quadlet template into per-kind scaffolds (.container/.pod/.network/.volume)

### AGY-1282 -- Add a single `just template-gate` recipe running the toolchain in strangler-fig order with a no-delete-before-parity guard  (WS-TEMPLATE | P2 | M)
**What+How:** The template work has hard ordering constraints the individual tasks don't encode: golden fixtures + workspace membership + fmt/clippy must land BEFORE the Rust ports; vocab/routing SSOT unification BEFORE `miosd scaffold`; and no python producer (mios-new, mios-template-engine, check-template-conformance, tools/compile-templates.py) may be DELETED until the Rust binary passes ALL golden fixtures byte-for-byte. Add a `just template-gate` target (and matching CI job) that runs compile-templates -> scaffold-every-registered-type -> check-template-conformance -> cross-repo parity in dependency order as ONE gate, plus a guard that FAILS if any listed python producer is removed while its golden-parity test is not green.
**Where:** `justfile (or Justfile), .github/workflows or automation CI entry, tools/compile-templates.py, usr/libexec/mios/{mios-new,check-template-conformance}`
**Done When:** `just template-gate` runs the four stages in order and is wired into CI; deleting a python producer without a green byte-parity fixture fails the guard; just drift-gate green.  **Why:** The campaign explicitly demands strangler-fig ordering (prove byte-parity, then delete); without a single ordered gate and a delete guard, a port could remove the fallback shim before the Rust replacement is proven, breaking scaffolding.  **Dep:** Capture golden-master fixtures + byte-parity harness for mios new across all registered types

## WS-PWSH -- PS AST parse-gate + decompose/compile the 36 PowerShell scripts  (AGY-1283..AGY-1318, 36 tasks)

### AGY-1283 -- Add a PowerShell AST parse-gate to CI (the single highest-value gate)  (WS-PWSH | P1 | M)
**What+How:** build-mios.ps1 was unparseable for ~70 commits undetected because no PS parse check runs in CI. audit_all.ps1 (lines 12-20) ALREADY implements the correct check via [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile but is never invoked by mios-ci.yml (its drift-gate job, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml lines 59-127, runs only lint-shell.sh/lint-python.sh/97-ssot-lint.sh/98-drift-checks.sh). Create automation/lint-powershell.sh mirroring lint-shell.sh's structure (SCRIPT_DIR/ROOT resolve, degrade-open exit 2 if pwsh absent, self-provision pwsh via apt/dnf best-effort) that globs every tracked *.ps1 and runs `pwsh -NoProfile -Command` calling Parser::ParseFile, failing on any parse error. Wire it as a new step in BOTH .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (drift-gate job, before 98-drift-checks) and .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml, and add a check_powershell_parse function to automation/98-drift-checks.sh so `just drift-gate` gates it locally too.
**Where:** `automation/lint-powershell.sh (new), automation/lint-shell.sh (pattern), audit_all.ps1, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml, .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** lint-powershell.sh exists and is invoked by both CI workflows + build.sh drift phase; deliberately breaking any .ps1 syntax fails the gate; a check_powershell_parse drift-check is registered; `bash automation/lint-powershell.sh` returns 0 on the clean tree and non-zero on an injected parse error; explicit paths staged (no git add -A).  **Why:** Recurring silent breakage (70 commits) proves the missing gate is the top hazard; the parser logic already exists in-repo, so this is pure wiring for enormous safety return.

### AGY-1284 -- Add a PSScriptAnalyzer static-analysis gate with a curated ruleset  (WS-PWSH | P1 | M)
**What+How:** MiOS has NO PowerShell static analysis (grep for Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer/PSScriptAnalyzer across the tree finds only doc mentions). Add automation/lint-ps-analyzer.sh that ensures the PSScriptAnalyzer module (Install-Module -Scope CurrentUser best-effort, degrade-open like lint-shell.sh) then runs `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Recurse -Settings automation/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` over all tracked *.ps1, failing on Error-severity findings. Author automation/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 as the clippy-equivalent curated ruleset (enable PSAvoidUsingInvokeExpression, PSAvoidUsingPlainTextForPassword, PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments, PSAvoidAssignmentToAutomaticVariable, PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions; start Warning-only for style rules to keep the tree green, Error for the security rules). Wire the step into .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml and .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml after the parse-gate.
**Where:** `automation/lint-ps-analyzer.sh (new), automation/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 (new), .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml, .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml`
**Done When:** Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer runs in both CI workflows against a committed settings file; injecting an Invoke-Expression on untrusted input fails the gate; the clean tree passes at the chosen severities; settings file + runner staged explicitly.  **Why:** clippy-style lint swap for the shell/PS world subsumes a whole bug class (Invoke-Expression injection, automatic-variable clobber, plaintext secrets) that the parse-gate alone cannot catch.  **Dep:** Add a PowerShell AST parse-gate to CI (the single highest-value gate)

## WS-SYSTEMD -- Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT + unit<->SSOT drift-check + sandboxing ratchet  (AGY-1319..AGY-1365, 47 tasks)

### AGY-1319 -- Fix stale mios-ai.target Wants=mios-letta-server.service and gate dangling unit refs  (WS-SYSTEMD | P1 | S)

Stage only the two edited files.
**Where:** `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-ai.target, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
**Done When:** mios-ai.target Wants only live units; new dangling-ref assertion inside check_dag_integrity FAILS on a synthetic bad edge and PASSES on the cleaned tree; `just drift-gate` (or bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh) green.  **Why:** A stale Wants= on a load-bearing target is a real boot-ordering hazard and a concrete SSOT/reality drift the compiled generator must never reintroduce; fixing it first gives the migration a clean DAG oracle.

SOFT-skip where podman is unavailable (off-Linux), matching the existing soft-gate pattern.
**Where:** `tools/generate-k3s-manifests.sh, usr/share/mios/k3s, usr/share/containers/systemd/*.pod, automation/98-drift-checks.sh, mios-unit-gen`
**Done When:** Changing a pod's membership or port in SSOT without re-projecting k3s fails the gate; a consistent regeneration passes; the check SOFT-skips without podman; drift-gate green on Linux/CI.  **Why:** The pods SSOT feeds TWO downstreams — Quadlets and k3s — and the generator work touches only the Quadlet side; without a consistency gate the cluster manifests become a silent third divergence surface the campaign is meant to prevent.  **Dep:** Subsume tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py into mios-unit-gen

### AGY-1441 -- Anchor the mios-hardcode-lint localhost:80 / :443 allowlist patterns so they stop masking real :80xx violations  (WS-ZEROHC | P1 | M)
**What+How:** In usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.nohc_allowlist].exempt_patterns (lines 842-861) the entries "localhost:80", "localhost:443", "127\.0\.0\.1:80", "127\.0\.0\.1:443" are consumed as UNANCHORED re.search patterns by mios-hardcode-lint (usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint lines 176-182 and 221-227 iterate exempt_rx and set is_line_exempt on the whole line). Because 'localhost:8090'/'8091'/'8033'/'8053'/'8080' all begin with the literal 'localhost:80', any line carrying those ports is spuriously exempted and its real hardcode goes unflagged. Fix by anchoring each to a non-digit lookahead: 'localhost:80(?![0-9])', 'localhost:443(?![0-9])', '127\.0\.0\.1:80(?![0-9])', '127\.0\.0\.1:443(?![0-9])'. This is a shared SSOT surface, so mirror the edit in BOTH usr/share/mios/mios.toml (mios.git) and C:/mios-bootstrap/mios.toml (Law 15). Land it COUPLED with the float edits it newly exposes (tasks that float :8090/:8091/:8033/:8053/:8080) so the gate goes green in the same PR rather than red on merge.
**Where:** `usr/share/mios/mios.toml (lines 842-861), C:/mios-bootstrap/mios.toml, usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint`
**Done When:** exempt_patterns anchored in both repos' mios.toml; running mios-hardcode-lint over a fixture line containing 'http://localhost:8090' now REPORTS the :8090 hardcode (previously PASS); the coupled float edits keep automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_no_hardcode green.  **Why:** This unanchored-allowlist bug is the single hazard that silently disarms the NO-HARDCODE gate for the entire :80xx published-port range (cockpit/cockpit_link/open_webui/adguard_ui/guacamole). Fixing it is the prerequisite that turns the zero-hardcodes campaign from advisory into enforced.

### AGY-1477 -- Add cosign signing to the Forgejo publisher to match GitHub (equal-publisher parity)  (WS-SBOM | P1 | M)
**What+How:** GitHub mios-ci.yml signs every pushed tag with keyless cosign (steps 'Install cosign'/'Cosign keyless sign', .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml lines 442-471), but grep for cosign/attest/sign in .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml returns NOTHING -- so Forgejo-published digests ship unsigned, breaking the release-topology 'GitHub is equal bit-for-bit publisher' invariant. Add a matching signing step to build-mios.yml: install cosign v2.x (see the cosign-v3 task), `source ./tools/lib/userenv.sh`, `cosign login` the registry host derived from MIOS_IMAGE_NAME (parity with the GitHub push-login), then `cosign sign --yes` each pushed tag. Forgejo has no GitHub OIDC issuer, so sign with the shared MIOS key (COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY secret, already referenced by generate-mok-key.sh's secrets note) to ONE identity policy; keep GitHub keyless. Mirror the workflow change in both mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15); stage explicit paths.
**Where:** `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (lines 442-471), tools/lib/userenv.sh`
**Done When:** build-mios.yml pushes then signs each published tag; `cosign verify` succeeds against a Forgejo-published digest; grep cosign in build-mios.yml is non-empty; drift-gate green; change present in both repos.  **Why:** An unsigned Forgejo publish silently violates the equal-publisher supply-chain guarantee the whole cutover depends on.

### AGY-1478 -- Unify the two divergent LUKS SSOT tables and make the recovery keyslot mandatory  (WS-SBOM | P1 | M)
**What+How:** Two conflicting LUKS config surfaces exist: usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen reads `[security.luks]` (enabled/pin/pcrs, mios.toml line 8745-8748) while usr/libexec/mios/mios-luks-enroll reads `config['security']['disk_encryption']` (mode/backend/pcrs/recovery, line 24-27) -- a table that does NOT exist in mios.toml, so mios-luks-enroll is a permanent no-op (mode defaults to 'none'). Collapse both consumers onto the single `[security.luks]` table (add `mode`, `backend`, `recovery` keys there), default pcrs to '7' (Secure-Boot-state; survives kernel/initramfs bumps unlike PCR0/9), and make the recovery keyslot UNCONDITIONAL -- today `recovery = de.get('recovery', True)` lets an operator set false and brick a fleet on any firmware/MOK change (enroll-mok.sh lines 207-213 warn about exactly this). Update automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_clevis_luks (line 4321) and add a check that mios-luks-enroll parses the unified table. Mirror the SSOT edit in both repos (Law 15); stage explicit paths.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-luks-enroll, usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen, usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.luks] (line 8745), automation/98-drift-checks.sh (line 4321)`
**Done When:** both tools read `[security.luks]`; mios-luks-enroll enrolls a recovery keyslot unconditionally and rejects recovery=false; no consumer references `[security.disk_encryption]`; drift-gate + negatives green; SSOT mirrored in both repos.  **Why:** Disk-unlock enrollment is currently dead code reading a nonexistent table, and a stray recovery=false could brick a whole fleet after a firmware update.

### AGY-1479 -- Pin CI cosign to v2.x legacy-attachment format so bootc policy can discover signatures  (WS-SBOM | P1 | S)
**What+How:** automation/49-cosign-policy.sh pins the in-image cosign to v2.x because 'v3+ breaks rpm-ostree OCI 1.1 bundle format' (header lines 11/25/32), yet CI installs `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3` (the v3 CLI, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml line 444) and signs with it -- cosign v3's new signing-bundle format is NOT discoverable by containers-image/rpm-ostree policy (bootc #528 / rpm-ostree #5509), so a strict sigstoreSigned policy would silently fail to verify CI signatures. Pin cosign-installer with `cosign-release: v2.6.4` (matching COSIGN_FALLBACK_VERSION in 49-cosign-policy.sh line 32) and/or export the legacy-attachment env so signatures land as sigstore attachments (the registries.d yamls already set `use-sigstore-attachments: true`). Apply identically to the new Forgejo signing step. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
**Where:** `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (lines 442-444, 451-471), automation/49-cosign-policy.sh (lines 11/25/32), .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml, usr/lib/containers/registries.d/`
**Done When:** CI signs with cosign v2.x; the pushed digest carries a `.sig` sigstore attachment (not a v3 referrers bundle) verifiable by rpm-ostree/containers-image policy; both workflows pinned; drift-gate green; Law 15 mirrored.  **Why:** Without this, every strict-policy verification (the next task) silently fails because the signatures are in a format bootc cannot read.

### AGY-1480 -- Generate a real sigstoreSigned policy.json from [security.sigstore] instead of insecureAcceptEverything  (WS-SBOM | P1 | M)
**What+How:** tools/generate-cosign-policy.py emits ONLY `{"default":[{"type":"insecureAcceptEverything"}]}` (the [security.sigstore].policy_mode default, mios.toml line 781-784) and the committed usr/lib/containers/policy.json matches -- so an immutable bootc host boots/upgrades into ANY image, the single highest-leverage boot-integrity gap. **Where:** `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py, usr/lib/containers/policy.json, usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.sigstore] (line 781), automation/49-cosign-policy.sh`
**Done When:** with policy_mode=sigstoreSigned the generated policy.json carries a sigstoreSigned rule keyed to the MiOS repo + mios-cosign.pub; `generate-cosign-policy.py --check` passes; `skopeo copy` admits a signed image and rejects an unsigned one under the policy; drift-gate green; mirrored in both repos.  **Why:** An immutable OS that trusts every image has no boot integrity; this converts signing effort into an actual enforcement gate.

**Done When:** `cosign verify-attestation --type spdx <published digest>` returns the SBOM predicate on both forges; CI step green; ADR-0003 doc updated to reference the attestation; Law 15 mirrored.  **Why:** An in-tree SBOM nobody can pull is not provenance; attesting it to the digest lets scanners verify the exact shipped bits.  **Dep:** Pin CI cosign to v2.x legacy-attachment format

### AGY-1483 -- Make the image build reproducible via git-derived SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + timestamp rewrite  (WS-SBOM | P2 | M)
**What+How:** The CI `sudo podman build` (.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml line 301-312) sets no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and no timestamp normalization, so file/layer mtimes vary run-to-run and a third party cannot reproduce the published digest -- contradicting the release-topology 'layer digests match bit-for-bit between publishers' invariant. Add `--timestamp "$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"` (and `--rewrite-timestamp` where buildah supports it) with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git -C "$ROOT" log -1 --format=%ct)` so the epoch is DETERMINISTIC and immune to build.sh's git-reset (per the drift-gate-local-verify memo's `/ IS $ROOT` note). Ensure base images are digest-pinned. Apply to both forges and to automation/build.sh where it drives the OCI build. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).

**Done When:** two independent CI builds of the same commit produce byte-identical image digests; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is git-commit-time derived; base images digest-pinned; both forges patched; Law 15 mirrored.  **Why:** Reproducible digests are the strongest supply-chain proof and the precondition for the two forges to publish provably-identical images.
